plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches in a short, dazzling display. Petals drift down like confetti at the end of the show. In northern Japan, the blooms draw crowds to parks and castle grounds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in central Japan, and mid-April to early May in northern Honshu and Hokkaido
plants.location: Tohoku and northern Honshu, Japan, where peak bloom often falls in mid-to-late April
plants.funFact: Yoshino cherries are clones. Nearly all of them come from grafting, so trees in the same area tend to bloom within days of each other.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every color stand on sturdy stems. In the Netherlands, bulb fields stretch to the horizon in bands of red, yellow, and purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May in the Netherlands, with peak bloom usually around mid-April
plants.location: Bulb region near Lisse, the Netherlands
plants.funFact: During the 1630s, tulip bulbs sold in the Netherlands for prices that rivaled those of grand houses. The episode is known as tulip mania.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Magenta-pink flowers burst straight from bare branches and even from the trunk. They appear before the heart-shaped leaves and make a bright show in woodland edges and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to late April, with peak bloom around mid-April in the mid-Atlantic and Midwest
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, including Virginia, Kentucky, and Missouri
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mild, tangy flavor. Bees rely on them as an early spring nectar source.
